citation.title: Evaluation of Esophageal Pressures in Mechanically Ventilated Obese Patients

provenance.quote: an openly available database composed of 53,423 distinct hospital admissions of adult patients admitted to critical care units of a tertiary care hospital between 2001 and 2012
The Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-III critical care database was queried to gather data on Pes in subjects on mechanical ventilation.
adult patients admitted to critical care units of a tertiary care hospital between 2001 and 2012
the Pes-guided PEEP and empirical PEEP protocols from the EPVent-2 trial4 were theoretically applied to all the subjects with obesity as well as those with class III obesity

the average Pes-guided PEEP would be 21.7 ± 5.2 cm H2O compared with the average empirical PEEP of 19.4 ± 3.2 cm H2O (P = .004). Furthermore, with the use of the Pes-guided protocol, the average end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure in these subjects who were obese would be 2.8 ± 2.3 cm H2O compared with 0.5 ± 6.2 cm H2O without Pes guidance (P < .001).
A total of 105 subjects were eventually included for the analysis.
The purpose of this study was to perform a retrospective analysis of Pes in subjects who were obese and on mechanical ventilation

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: obesity_subgroup: the full cohort spans BMI < 30 to > 60 kg/m2 (44 non-obese, 61 obese, 20 class III), so mixed_bmi; the theoretical PEEP application was restricted to the obese groups. ards_subgroup: an unselected ventilated population; ARDS status not reported ('We are unable to make any remarks on whether Pes guidance would improve outcomes in patients who are obese and on mechanical ventilation with or without ARDS'). timing_subgroup: Pes measurement occurred a median of 3 days after admission, but no intervention was delivered, so early/late classification is not meaningful. ptp_target_subgroups: the EPVent-2 Pes-guided protocol targets positive end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure via absolute Pes subtraction. Mortality ranking: in-hospital mortality is the only mortality outcome reported, so it carries is_longest_reported_mortality.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No overlap with any cohort in COHORTS.md. This is a retrospective analysis of the MIMIC-III database (de-identified admissions 2001–2012 from a tertiary care hospital); it delivers no intervention and shares no patients with EPVent-2 (beitler_2019), EPVent-1 (talmor_2008), or any prospective cohort in the pool. It merely applies the EPVent-2 PEEP protocols in simulation. Compared registration (none for this study), enrolment window (database period 2001–2012), and population (unselected MIMIC-III ventilated subjects, obese and non-obese).
unclear_items: eligibility.criteria.balloon_guided_peep_titration: coded 'no' — the EPVent-2 PEEP protocols were applied only theoretically to charted MIMIC-III data; no ventilator setting was ever changed in a patient (consistent with the COHORTS.md eligibility flag).
design.countries: inferred United States from the Cleveland Clinic, Ohio affiliation and the MIMIC-III database (US tertiary care hospital); the paper does not state a country.

outcomes[transpulmonary_pressure].paired_effects: the text reports P < .001 for the obese-group end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure contrast while Table 3 reports P = .008 for the same contrast; both recorded, table value used as p_value.

outcomes[mortality].data: events per group derived from reported percentages and denominators (32.8% of 61, 47.7% of 44, 30% of 20); the paper reports percentages, not event counts, except the cohort total 41/105.

design.comparison_structure: coded within_patient_crossover because the review-relevant contrast (empirical vs Pes-guided PEEP) applies two hypothetical protocols to the same subjects; the obese vs non-obese Pes comparison is between different patients and is captured as separate arms with effect_estimates.
design.enrolment_start/enrolment_end: set to the MIMIC-III database coverage period (2001–2012), which is when the underlying admissions occurred, not a study-specific enrolment window.
population.age/sex/bmi cohort-level fields left null because Table 1 reports characteristics only per group; recorded in baseline_by_arm instead.

intervention.peep_titration_target: the EPVent-2 numeric end-expiratory Ptp target range is not restated in this paper; only 'positive transpulmonary pressure' is stated, so the numeric low/high targets are null.
data_only_in_figure: Fig. 1: box plots of esophageal pressure distributions (obese vs non-obese; class III obesity vs non-obese) — medians/IQRs not otherwise tabulated
Fig. 2: box plots of theoretical PEEP under empirical vs Pes-guided protocols in all obese subjects and class III obesity subgroup
extraction_flags.general_notes: Simulation-only study: no esophageal balloon was placed by these authors and no ventilator setting was changed; excluded from the review (balloon_not_used_to_guide_peep) but extracted for the adjudicator. Pes was not directly charted — it was back-calculated as total PEEP minus charted end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure. Additional reported findings with no dedicated field: end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure negative in 44% (27/61) of obese subjects and 65% (13/20) of class III subjects under empirical PEEP; Pes > 24 cm H2O in 4.9% (2/41) non-obese, 13.1% (8/61) obese, and 20% (4/20) class III subjects; BMI–Pes correlation Pearson r = 0.29, P = .002; overall cohort in-hospital mortality 39% (41/105); class III empirical-PEEP end-expiratory Ptp range −17 to 3 cm H2O.
